title: Overwrite IndexSearcher#slices method for multi threaded search

timeline.message: Overwrite IndexSearcher#slices method for multi threaded search
timeline.author: iverase

timeline.body:
The implementation ensures that each slice contains at least 10% of the documents on the index and that the number of slices won't be bigger that the number of available threads. In addition it set a minim number of documents per slice regardless, hardcoded to 50k documents.

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/97270
Pinging @elastic/es-search (Team:Search)

timeline.author: iverase

timeline.body: just a nit, and bare with me I haven't reviewed code in quite some time.  Here is my question, wouldn't it be simpler to initialize the group on top and remove the null check to simplify the loop. I might need to rewire my brain for some time so I might miss obvious things :D

reply.body:
Hello Simon, I am sure you will be as sharp as before in no time :)

You are right, the loop looks a bit simpler without lazy initialising the group array list. Changed it accordingly.

timeline.body: inc the `upto` here?

just a question, would it make sense to think about the number of documents as a result of a query/filter.count() and drop slices ahead of time in the case of a match none? I am just trying to think about cases where decisions can be made much more efficient like with a sampling run of a cheap query. We don't need to add this now but for the future it might be something we wanna expose?
Maybe just use `RandomIndexWriter`

reply.body: I changed to use the RIW and simplified the test quite a bit, thanks!

timeline.body: if you use RIW you can drop that part
maybe use some random number instead of that exhaustive loop and loop over a random number as iterations. This might catch issues when the same number is use multiple times etc.

reply.body: Changed for a random number of iterations

timeline.body: also this might happen in RIW
I like the change, I left some comments and nits. mainly to get back in to the game here. bare with me. I think others should still review it because I might not have all the context. /cc @javanna

timeline.author: iverase
iverase

timeline.body: @elasticmachine run elasticsearch-ci/part-2
lets also rarely do something like this: `rarely() ? randomIntBetween(0, 1000) : randomIntBetween(1000, 25000);`

reply.body: good point, I have actually check manually the behaviour for 0 documents and as expected it returns an empty array.

timeline.body: can you add an assert that `numThreads` is never 0? I think we should actually throw an exception if its less than `1` to be honest. and also have a test for it

reply.body: in other words pls. fix the division by zero potential here
Added an explicit check and added to the tests.

timeline.body: thanks for pushing changes @iverase I left some more smaller comments. LGTM otherwise

+highlight:
+  title: Asset tracking - geo_line in time-series aggregations
+  body: |-
+    The <<search-aggregations-metrics-geo-line,`geo_line` aggregation>> builds tracks from `geo_points`.
+    It has previously needed to use large arrays in memory for collecting points into multiple buckets
+    and sorting those buckets.
+
+    With the advances made in TSDB features and the `time_series` aggregation in particular,
+    it is now possible to rely on data aggregating in both TSID and timestamp order,
+    enabling the removal of all sorting, as well as the use of only a single bucket's
+    worth of memory, a dramatic improvement in memory footprint. In addition, we can use the streaming line
+    simplifier algorithm introduced in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/94859 to replace the previous
+    behaviour of truncating very large tracks with the far more preferable approach of simplifying those tracks.
+
+    [role="screenshot"]
+    image:images/spatial/kodiak_geo_line_simplified.png[North short of Kodiak Island simplified to 100 points]
+
+    In this diagram, the grey line is the original geometry, the blue line is the truncated geometry as would be
+    produced by the original `geo_line` aggregation, and the magenta line is the new simplified geometry.
+  notable: false

timeline.body: Maybe a silly question: what does `getPoolSize` give us? the number of threads in the pool? Isn't that the total number of threads, regardless of how many are available vs active? That is supposed to be an upper bound though?

reply.body:
The current issue says: 
```
A maximum number of slices. The number of slices that a shard level search creates should be capped. To avoid creating more slices than available search threads.
```
So I am reading `available search threads` as the pool size regardless if the thread is already executing another task.

to me available == active , but I may be wrong. On the other hand, I am not sure if we will after all tie the number of slices to the number of threads. Maybe for now we should just cap it to something like 10, and later we can refine it.

I think we should use `ThreadPoolExecutor#getPoolSize(...)` as basis to determine the `maxSliceNum` here. I think `ThreadPoolExecutor#getActiveCount(...)` can vary quickly over time and I think it is ok of a thread executes multiple slice searches? At the time we attempt to fork we really know whether there is a search thread available to perform a slice search. But basing the number of slices on `ThreadPoolExecutor#getActiveCount(...)` makes `maxSliceNum` not predictable. The `maxSliceNum` is a maximum, but I think it is good to let it be based on the search thread pool size (size that is based on the number cores) compared to a static value. Maybe we should `maxSliceNum` based on `ThreadPoolExecutor#getPoolSize(...) / 2` to always be conservative on the maximum number of slices.
I agree that maybe limited down to half of the pool size might avoid greedy searches using all the pool.

timeline.body:
It looks good to me.

One possible improvement for a follow-up: it is common to filter on recent data, which would more commonly be stored in the smaller segments. So it may help queries filtered by time if we could enforce that the smaller segments are not all in the same slice, which the current packing algorithm doesn't try to do unless I'm missing something.
